name: Quotatank
author: JanitorHead
description: Menu-bar AI usage tracker and monitor for coding agents. Shows how much of your Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (ChatGPT), Gemini CLI, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Kimi, Grok, Kiro, Z.ai GLM, MiniMax or OpenCode subscription is left: 5-hour and weekly rate limits, quotas, resets, pace. Tracks prepaid credits and balances for OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Moonshot and more. Finds your sign-ins on its own. A Costs tab charts tokens and LLM spend per model, like ccusage.

schema.label: Quota source
schema.description: Read local CLI sign-ins or query Fusebox and CLIProxyAPI accounts. Proxy implementations are detected automatically. Costs has its own source setting.

schema.label: Fusebox / CLIProxyAPI server URL
schema.description: Server, management.html, or /v0/management URL. HTTPS certificates are verified.

schema.label: Proxy management key file
schema.description: Managed automatically by the settings menu when saving a Management API key. Advanced users can supply an existing private key file path here.

schema.label: Hide account emails
schema.description: Replace account usernames and email addresses with numbered labels and hide account identity in settings.

schema.label: Square usage cards
schema.description: Use square corners for cards in Limits instead of the theme's corner style.

schema.label: Provider colors
schema.description: Color each provider's bar chip and limit meters with its brand color instead of the Omarchy theme colors. The cost chart always uses provider colors.

schema.label: Notify when limits run low
schema.description: Send a desktop notification when a limit moves into the warning or critical threshold. Recovering and a reset re-arm the next notification.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: How often provider usage is refreshed. Manual refresh is always available.

schema.label: Providers
schema.description: Select providers to monitor in local mode. Providers with a sign-in of their own appear once you sign in; API-key providers need a key saved in settings or set in the environment. Fusebox and CLIProxyAPI discover all managed providers automatically.

schema.label: Provider order
schema.description: Set by dragging providers under Settings → Providers. JSON array of provider IDs; listed providers come first in that order in tiles, chips, and provider cycling, the rest follow.

schema.label: Providers not suggested
schema.description: Managed under Settings → Providers. Providers found on this computer that you chose not to monitor, so they are not suggested again. Turning a provider on removes it from this list.

schema.label: Bar display
schema.description: Percentages shows compact quota on horizontal bars and falls back to the icon on vertical bars.

schema.label: Show limits as
schema.description: Whether limit cards and menu bar chips report the percentage used or the percentage left; balances follow it too. The warning thresholds always apply to what is left. One provider can be read the other way under Display → Per provider.

schema.label: Show limits as, per provider
schema.description: Managed under Display → Per provider in settings. JSON object mapping provider IDs to Used or Remaining; missing providers follow Show limits as.

schema.label: Menu bar: limit shown
schema.description: Which reported limit supplies the menu bar percentage. Most constrained uses the window with the least remaining quota; a provider that does not report the chosen window falls back to that.

schema.label: Menu bar: second limit below
schema.description: Optional second limit stacked under the first in each menu bar chip. none keeps a single line.

schema.label: Menu bar: show when limits reset
schema.description: Adds when each chip's limit resets. Limits that reset within a day show a time; weekly and monthly limits show a date.

schema.label: Menu bar: hide providers with a used-up weekly or monthly limit
schema.description: Removes a provider's chip while one of its weekly or monthly limits is used up. The chip returns when that limit resets; Limits keeps showing the provider.

schema.label: Menu bar: most chips shown (0 = all)
schema.description: Past this many, the bar keeps the providers closest to a limit and folds the rest into a +N chip.

schema.label: Menu bar: reset time format
schema.description: Time format for limits that reset within a day, such as the 5-hour session limit: 24-hour (14:30) or 12-hour (2:30 PM).

schema.label: Menu bar: reset date format
schema.description: Date format for weekly and monthly limit resets: DD/MM (22/04), MM/DD (04/22) or D MMM (22 Apr).

schema.label: Menu bar: per-provider limits
schema.description: Managed under Providers → Customize in settings. JSON object mapping provider IDs to top and bottom bar limits; missing slots use the limits chosen for all providers.

schema.label: Menu bar providers
schema.description: Enabled providers allowed to show percentage chips in the menu bar. Hidden providers remain in the popup.

schema.label: Low balance warning (USD)
schema.description: Warn when the money a prepaid balance can still spend falls to this amount or below, in the balance's own currency.

schema.label: Low balance critical (USD)
schema.description: Critical when the money left falls to this amount or below. Must not be above the warning amount.

schema.label: Custom model prices
schema.description: Managed by Custom model prices in Costs settings. Exact model IDs mapped to USD-per-million input/output and optional cache rates as JSON.

schema.label: CPA Usage Keeper URL
schema.description: Optional Keeper URL for Go proxy account activity. Fusebox reports activity directly. Not used for Costs.

schema.label: Keeper password file
schema.description: Managed privately when saving the Keeper login password in settings. Advanced users can supply a private password file.

schema.label: T3 Code cost servers
schema.description: Managed by Costs settings. Remote servers with private token file references.

schema.label: Live account activity
schema.description: Use one shared Fusebox stream for requests serving now. Older Rust proxies show unavailable activity.
